Results.ReviewText: Purchased on an online merchant. The grill arrived very quickly. I signed up for free assembly and that worked out great. There was a problem though, there were about 3 or 4 parts that were banged up. After calling and talking with a service rep. she gave me to a supervisor. The supervisor was fantastic, she registered my grill so they could over night the parts. The parts arrived very quickly and the assembly men came back and quickly finished the assembly. The grill works great and I can see the difference from my old grill to the new weber grill. The grill was a great buy and would do it all over again. Weber has excellent customer service.

Results.ReviewText:
I have used the grill about 7 or 8 times cooking steaks and burgers. I am disappointed that the grill simply does not get hot enough to provide the searing of the meat you would expect it to accomplish.  I have turned it on the highest level and preheated for 30 minutes.  The thermometer never goes above 400 degrees.

It will cook items eventually but it does not get as hot as I think it should and it takes twice as long to cook items.  We had friends over and cooked burgers. I cooked them about 20 minutes on high and they were still raw in the middle. It was embarrassing to say the least because they wanted well done and I thought 20 minutes would do the job.  The burgers were about 3/4 of an inch thick. I should have cut into them before serving but thought 20 minutes was sufficient.

Results.ReviewText:
We are very happy with the BBQ, just got the 2 burner since there are only 2 of us -- we don't need anything bigger.  

The only thing we don't understand is the extra large round hole in the bottom of the cabinet.  It's too large for a 20 lb. propane tank, and there are no inserts for it to make it fit.  When I called your Customer Service department, the only explanation they could come up with is that is for "ventilation"!  Huh?  There are ventilation slits on 3 sides of the paneling, so that doesn't make any sense.  And the idea of trying to hang a 20 lb. tank from the tiny hook inside is ridiculous -- I can't lift something that heavy up there.  We ended up buying a "box" to sit outside the BBQ that holds the tank.  Not what we had in mind when we purchased this BBQ.  We intentionally wanted the one with a cabinet so we could set the propane tank inside.  Maybe your engineers (designers) can make a slide out tray that fits inside the cabinet, so the tank can be stored out of sight!!!

Results.ReviewText: I have used every cheap(er) brand of grill on the market and honestly didn't think it could possibly be worth it to even look at more expensive ones. I figured I could buy 10 $100 grills over the course of 40 or so years before I had spent what a Weber would cost. Once I sat down with my 6th or 7th grill and realized I was spending more like $350-$400 each time and still having to replace them every few years I decided it had not been a wise financial choice if a better grill would last. My neighbor had a weber that was something like 25 years  old and still going strong. I went and looked at the smaller weber grills and sure enough for $350 I could get a solid grill, that isn't going to rust out and it had virtually the same cooking area as my last grill, By the time I had this thing assembled I already knew I had made the right choice!
Results.Title: So much more quality than my old grills!

Results.ReviewText:
The grill is ok , takes a long time to assemble and the door is a piece of junk if you pull hard the door falls off.
Not he quality I thought I would get with a Weber
Results.Title: Grill is ok,

Results.ReviewText: We bought this Grill when we built our new house 3 years ago. We thought the warranty was great, but we didn't do enough research. Don't get me wrong, I love Webber and I've had many, many Webber products, but I've never experienced so many issues. With very light use for our family of 3 (1x week most of the spring, summer and fall) this grill should last. It's covered constantly and cleaned with every use. However, if I were to do it again, stainless is the only way to go for the grates. I repeat, DO NOT BUY THIS GRILL, until they come out with a stainless grate option. The grates need to be replaced every year, even with good cleaning using Webber products. I just wish I would have went with the Genesis line for the stainless steel option. Once again this year I will be spending almost $70 on new grates.
Results.Title: Keep Looking... stainless is your friend.

Results.ReviewText:
I debated whether to buy a lessor priced grill or go with the Weber. I wanted a two burner due to just two in the family. After talking to multiple employees at Lowe’s they said how many grills at this price have a 10 year warranty? Bottom line, Weber grills are more sturdy. The materials used are stronger and should last longer. 
The only issue I have is the base for the gas tank could be a better design instead of a plastic base. Without the separate base the tank has to be removed to move the grill. 
I highly recommend this grill
Results.Title: Built to last

46110001.Name: Spirit E-210 Gas Grill (Liquid Propane)
46110001.Description:
Taste the difference a Spirit will make in your life. With features such as porcelain enameled, cast-iron cooking grates that retain even heat, you’re guaranteed the best tasting food. It’s built to last with a cookbox that helps prevent rusting and peeling, and conveniently equipped with six tool hooks for easy accessibility of grilling tools. If that wasn’t enough, the low maintenance and easy-to-clean grease management system takes the hassle out of cooking. Designed to fit on a small patio or balcony, the Spirit E-210 gas grill brings grilling to any home.


• Durable, easy-to-clean porcelain-enamel cast iron grates.

• Porcelain-enameled finish helps prevent rusting and pealing.

• Six tool hooks for easy accessibility of grilling tools.

• Low maintenance and easy-to-clean grease management system.

• 360 square inches of main grilling space.


 This product requires assembly.
